summary.headline: KRBL Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,727 crore (+14% YoY) on a 33% domestic surge, while exports fell 41% in H1 on Middle East disruption.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was KRBL's highest-ever quarterly revenue, driven by domestic branded consumer packs (volume +18% YoY per management, with a later +19% figure) and a selective INR102 crore bulk rice sale. Exports remained the weak spot: H1 export revenue was INR541 crore (-41%), almost entirely from bulk exports to the Middle East, though Q2 exports rose 22% QoQ to INR297 crore. PAT was INR159 crore (14.6% margin) versus INR172 crore (11.2%) a year earlier, and cash plus treasury investments rose to INR2,895 crore. Management guided Q3 EBITDA of 16-20% and FY27 EBITDA of 17-19%, with paddy prices up sharply for the new crop.

segments.name: Domestic (India business)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue ex-power INR1,390 crore in Q2 (+33% YoY); H1 INR2,612 crore (+24%). Branded rice INR1,134 crore (+23%); unbranded INR166 crore including a one-off INR102 crore bulk sale.

segments.name: Branded consumer packs
segments.commentary: Consumer pack volume growth accelerated to 18% in Q2 from 7% in Q1; modern trade and e-commerce +31%, general trade +10% after a ~5% decline in Q1. Bulk packs +11% YoY in Q2; regional rice +42% in Q2, +32% in H1.

segments.name: Export (bulk and branded)
segments.commentary: H1 export revenue INR541 crore (-41%), driven by bulk exports to the Middle East; branded exports +18% in H1 and non-Middle East exports +14% in H1. Bulk sales in H1 described as almost zero.

segments.name: Edible oil and masala
segments.commentary: Uplife oil Q2 turnover about INR6 crore; masala H1 sales about INR4.5 crore vs INR3.1 crore, with a FY27 exit run-rate ambition of about INR25 crore.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 16-20%, with management saying it could be near 20%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 17-19%.
Domestic rice volume growth of about 10% YoY targeted for FY27 (H2 specifically); management said the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise.
Domestic price increases of about 7-8% in Q3 on average (management), after earlier cited 15-18% on specific price points.

Exports expected to recover progressively in H2 FY27, dependent on Gulf conditions; management said FY27 exports could match or beat last year's roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore, and the analyst's INR7,500 crore revenue / 16-17% PAT scenario was described as feasible if exports recover.
If the US-Iran situation settles, bulk exports could more than double, with management citing 30,000-40,000 tons or more; Iran previously ~100,000 tons a year.

qa_highlights.question: What export and volume growth is expected from here, and would exports double if the US-Iran situation settles?
qa_highlights.answer: Anil Mittal said exports could more than double once a US-Iran agreement is reached, with bulk sales (near zero in H1) possibly reaching 30,000-40,000 tons or more. Ayush Gupta reiterated about 10% domestic volume growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected in Q3 given the low-cost inventory and higher paddy prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Anoop Gupta guided Q3 EBITDA of 16-20%, saying old-crop stock earns higher margins and new-crop margins will be lower; he later said the figure would be nearing 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 vs Q1 volume growth, and why did gross margin fall from 33.5% to 32.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Jain cited 18% QoQ rice volume growth and 18% QoQ domestic growth, and attributed the margin dip to lower forex and treasury gains in other income, with higher freight and advertising costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation for domestic and export sales and the Q3 price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic realisation was about INR80/kg and exports about INR132/kg. Management said Q3 domestic prices would be about 7-8% higher on average, after earlier citing 15-18% increases.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR7,500 crore with a 16-17% PAT margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Jain said H1 revenue was about INR3,200 crore. He said the scenario looks feasible only if H2 exports recover to at least the prior year's roughly INR1,550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick commerce contribution, the Middle East outlook, and capital return plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce is 8-9% of India business with a 41.1% share. Anoop Gupta said a buyback could be considered and the company would discuss it internally. The dividend policy is 15% of profit, with management indicating it could exceed that.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on the Strait of Hormuz, freight and war-risk premiums, and banking channels; Iran is largely shut due to tighter US sanctions since August.
Paddy inflation (about 20% YoY) may compress margins as new-crop costs flow through, even with price increases of about 7-8% in Q3.
Consumer pack sustainability in H2 and whether the 18-19% Q2 volume growth holds; the India Gate price increase may trigger a shift to loose rice or smaller packs.
Uplife edible oil availability on e-commerce platforms; management said e-commerce sales are slow and investment needs are high.
Sub-judice ED matter, on which management declined to take questions.
Monsoon-linked crop estimates (basmati crop reported modestly above last year, with October rain damage) and possible next-year weather risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic momentum and pricing, but cautious on exports, which management tied explicitly to Gulf developments. Specific numbers were often given as ranges, and a few answers were hedged or unclear (e.g., Q3 margin range, the buyback response).
key_quotes: As I said last quarter, this remains a logistics problem and not a demand problem.
We would rather protect the quality to our business than chase volume.
We will not chase the market.
Our inventory is not for the quarter. Our inventory for another one and a half year.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity expansion or commissioning timeline was discussed on the call.

Procurement: paddy procurement planned at about 750,000 tons for FY27, with paddy prices up about 20% YoY (Anoop Gupta); buying staggered across the season with focus on low moisture, high recovery paddy.
Inventory at 30 Sep 2026: paddy 31,000 tons (vs 33,000 tons a year earlier) and rice 278,000 tons (vs 304,000 tons); management said inventory extends about one and a half years for some SKUs.

Distribution: India Gate present in about 3.3 lakh outlets and reaches about 1.2 crore urban households; order-to-cash programme under way to link order placement, stock allocation, collections and claims; work on availability in under-penetrated towns.
Export go-to-market: management decided against opening its own office in Saudi Arabia, preferring distributors; Africa (South Africa) cited as a growth area.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 consumer pack volume growth was 18% YoY (Ayush Gupta later gave 19% YoY for Q2 rice volumes); Q1 was 7%. Modern trade and e-commerce consumer pack volumes +31%; general trade +10% after about 5% decline in Q1. Bulk packs +11% YoY in Q2, October described as another strong month; regional rice +42% in Q2, +32% in H1.

Domestic realisation about INR80/kg in both Q1 and Q2 FY27, about 12% higher than Q2 FY26. Export realisation about INR132/kg in Q2. Price increases taken across the portfolio in Q3: management said 7-8% on average, after earlier citing 15-18% on specific price points.

Market share (12 months to September): India Gate about 36% in general trade (nearly twice the next player), 39.6% in modern trade, and internal estimate of 41.1% in e-commerce exit share in September versus about 33% for the next player; quick commerce is 8-9% of the India business.

Export demand: H1 bulk exports to the Middle East near zero; branded exports +18% in H1; non-Middle East exports +14% in H1. Management said Saudi Arabia steady; Iran shut for banking reasons after August US sanctions; if the US-Iran situation settles, bulk exports could rise more than double, with 30,000-40,000 tons or more cited. Management also cited Iran's earlier level of about 100,000 tons a year.

Global and Indian basmati context: basmati paddy trading at INR4,500-5,200 per quintal, with 1509 and 1121 varieties up at least INR1,000 per quintal YoY; non-basmati prices up about 30%; FY27 export volumes for India basmati Apr-Aug at 2.5 million tons vs 2.7 million tons a year earlier, with realisations about 21% higher in rupee terms.

Guidance: domestic rice volume growth of about 10% for FY27 (H2 focus), with management saying the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise; FY27 exports expected to match or beat the prior year's roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore; FY27 EBITDA 17-19%; Q3 EBITDA 16-20%, with management later saying it would be nearing 20%.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 domestic volume growth of about 10% (H2-weighted) and FY27 EBITDA margin of 17-19%, with Q3 EBITDA of 16-20%; backing is demand/share gains (consumer pack volume +18% in Q2, 36% general-trade share), price increases of 7-8% in Q3, and paddy procurement of 750,000 tons, but no capacity additions or capex were discussed and export recovery depends on Gulf conditions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q3 EBITDA guided at 16-20% (nearing 20%) versus 21.1% in Q2, with 7-8% Q3 price increases offset by paddy inflation of about 20% and lower treasury gains; FY27 EBITDA guided at 17-19%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 10% domestic rice volume growth for FY27 (H2-weighted) after 18-19% in Q2 and 7% in Q1, backed by 36% general-trade share and modern trade/e-commerce volume +31%, though management said the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity expansion was discussed on the call; the brief lists capex_read as not discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 exports could match or beat roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore and bulk exports could more than double if US-Iran settles (30,000-40,000 tons cited), but this depends on Gulf developments.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Exports (H1 INR541 crore, -41%) hinge on Gulf conditions, and paddy prices up about 20% YoY could compress margins as new-crop costs flow through, against FY27 EBITDA guidance of 17-19%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Masala ambition to exit FY27 at an annualised run rate of about INR25 crore, versus H1 sales of about INR4.5 crore; no new product launches were named.

rows.label: Q3 domestic price increase of 7-8%
rows.why: Price increases were taken across the portfolio in Q3, averaging 7-8% after earlier citing 15-18% on specific price points, against paddy prices up about 20% YoY.

rows.label: Possible buyback
rows.why: Anoop Gupta said a buyback could be considered and would be discussed internally, with no decision given; dividend policy is 15% of profit and could exceed that.

rows.label: Africa (South Africa) export growth
rows.why: Management cited Africa as a growth area and chose distributors over an own Saudi office, but gave no volume or revenue figures.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic volume, share and pricing, but cautious on exports, which it tied to Gulf and US-Iran developments; analysts pressed on Q3 margin range, FY27 revenue/PAT scenario, and buyback response, which were answered with ranges or hedges.
